description.narrative: The project’s primary goal is to support grassroots community organisations (CBOs) and self-help groups (SHGs) within Croix-des-Bouquets communities experiencing the most significant deterioration in food security over the past three years due to gang violence, accumulated rainfall deficits throughout the spring 2023 season, and a significant economic slowdown for four consecutive years. The general problems faced by the commune, such as insecurity, rising food prices, etc., are beyond the scope and capacity of the communal sections (Varreux 1, Beudet & Varreux 2, Depio). However, community members can come together to solve issues that specifically affect their community, such as maintaining drainage channels to prevent flooding. These channels, which are simple open ditches dug into the ground for rainwater drainage, are usually clogged with silt and waste (mostly plastic), preventing them from functioning properly. The needs and interests of all groups remain the same: safety of lives and property, food security, availability and accessibility of services, disaster risk management, etc. The project objective is to utilize the SCLR approach to adopt more sustainable practices and mitigate the impacts of anthropogenic activities on their environment and livelihoods in Croix-des-Bouquets, commune of the West department of Haiti. The project aims to support communities in their initiatives to waste management and cleaning of drainage system to mitigate the adverse impacts of flooding. The recognized vulnerability to flooding in this commune, located in a plain, makes this project a priority, especially as the implementation timeline coincides with the 2024 hurricane season. The project aims to directly assist at least 100 vulnerable families, comprising approximately 500 individuals, by providing direct funding to CBOs/Self-Help Groups for the implementation of their priority initiatives within their respective communities. These families will be identified among the IDPs and vulnerable communities dependent on cross-border trade and employment opportunities. Identified vulnerable and marginalized groups include internally displaced people, people living with disabilities, children, single mothers, older individuals, pregnant and/or lactating women.
